name: Tarnish-Void
geological_features: Tarnished mineral surfaces covering broad plains
Massive canyon systems exposing geological history
specific_features: Colony settlement destroyed by unknown event
description: Tarnish-Void is a barren world that wears the evidence of its decline in the oxidized, tarnished surfaces that cover its broad mineral plains. The planet's thin atmosphere, insufficient to support complex life, preserves just enough air to carry dust and to slowly oxidize the exposed minerals into muted browns, greens, and blacks. Dry riverbeds and empty ocean basins tell of a world that once held water, and the canyon walls display the geological record of its loss in stark, readable layers.

The world has the feel of a place that has been emptied out, a container from which the contents have been removed. The thin air carries a metallic taste and supports a wan, yellowish sky that gives everything a jaundiced appearance. Wind moves through the canyons and across the plains with a soft moan, the only sound on a world that seems to have been abandoned by everything, including hope. The tarnished surfaces give the landscape a used quality, like a tool that has been worked until it can give no more.

A colony was established here when the planet's water loss was thought to be reversible through terraforming. Atmospheric processors were installed, water extraction from subsurface ice began, and for two decades the colony grew. Then, in a single night according to survivor testimony, the colony was destroyed by an event that no one can adequately describe: structures collapsed, equipment failed simultaneously, and the atmospheric processors reversed their function, stripping rather than building the atmosphere. The survivors were evacuated, and no one has returned to investigate.

The destroyed colony remains untouched, a ghost settlement on a dying world. The terraforming equipment continues to strip the atmosphere at a rate that will render the planet completely airless within a century, but no one has been willing to approach close enough to shut it down. The event that destroyed the colony remains officially unexplained, though unofficial theories range from sabotage to the activation of dormant alien technology to the planet itself rejecting modification. Whatever the truth, Tarnish-Void serves as a cautionary tale about the limits of terraforming.
